content:
Carla N: @channel FYI BlueCart (tenant bc-918) is seeing repeated 429s + token latency spikes on their dedicated pool (dedicated-eu-west-1). Started ~21:10 UTC, still happening. They report lots of scale up/down churn.
Carla N: Sample from their app logs: ```2026-03-16T21:12:03Z ERROR request=rc-447 429 throttle: no capacity available
2026-03-16T21:12:05Z WARN request=rc-448 latency_ms=1200 kv_cache_miss=true
``` They also saw occasional auth errors but mostly 429s. Attaching request ids in a sec.
Samir R: oncall here — can you paste a couple request ids and tenant id? Any billing anomalies? Also @Priya please watch the autoscaler dashboards.
Carla N: tenant=bc-918
request_ids: rc-447, rc-448, rc-459
No billing alerts in the console.
SupportBot: Incident created ICS-2026-1123 by Carla N
Priya (sre-oncall): Looking at autoscaler events — I see a pattern: rapid scale-ups followed by scale-downs within ~90s. scale_up at 21:11:40 -> scale_down at 21:13:10 -> scale_up at 21:14:00. That's classic oscillation.
Alex L: Can you share runtime metrics for that pool? GPU util, queued requests, inflight token rate, and sampler of 95/99 latency? I suspect bursty queueing causing spikes that trigger the scaler then cooldown cuts capacity.
Carla N: Pasted Grafana links in thread DM. Quick snap from their timeseries: 95p latency jumps to 1.4s on bursts, GPU util hits 85% at peak then drops to 20% after scale-down.
Samir R: Root-cause hypothesis: noisy neighbor or bursty client traffic -> autoscaler reacts to short high-percentile latency -> scale completes -> traffic drops (or cache warms) -> downscale too fast -> repeat. Also saw kv_cache_miss rate higher for bc-918.
Alex L: Agreed. Immediate mitigations we can apply:
- Increase scale-down cooldown from 60s -> 300s for that pool (reduces thrash)
- Switch smoothing policy to moving-average over 3m for the scale metric
- Temporarily set min_replicas=2 for the tenant's shard
- If urgent, pin tenant to reserved capacity or add +1 GPU to pool
Samir R: Also recommend enabling request smoothing at the routing layer: simple token-bucket per-tenant to smooth bursts (ex: 50 qps sustained, 200 qps burst with 30s refill). That prevents tiny spikes from tripping scaler.
Carla N: BlueCart is ok with temporary capacity bump if it stabilizes them quickly. Maria T (CS) copied.
Maria T: I'll ask BlueCart if they can do short-term rate limiting on their side (client backoff). But they want platform-side fix first.
Priya (sre-oncall): Repro steps for engineering — to simulate their pattern:
1) Run burst load: 100 rps for 30s, then idle 30s, repeat 10x
2) Use sample curl: ```for i in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood/dedicated/bc-918 & done``` (wrap in loop)
3) Measure 95/99 latency and scaler events
Samir R: Action items:
- Priya: increase scale-down cooldown to 300s on dedicated-eu-west-1 pool for bc-918 (temporary) — ETA 15m
- Alex: enable 3m smoothing on scale metric and set min_replicas=2 for tenant — ETA 30m
- Eng-runtime (Alex): investigate KV cache miss pattern and whether cold-KV warming would help — follow-up in 24h
- Maria: coordinate with BlueCart for client-side burst control — keep us posted
Carla N: I'll notify the customer that we're applying temporary capacity+cooldown and will follow up.
Alex L: Quick note: if throttles persist after cooling changes, we'll plan a controlled capacity increase and consider tenant isolation (migrate to private shard) — that requires ops lead but is doable.
Priya (sre-oncall): Changes applied: scale-down cooldown=300s and min_replicas=2 on shard bc-918. Monitoring now. I'll post updates.
Carla N: thx. I'll mark support ticket with the mitigations and expected follow-up window.
Maria T: noted, updating BlueCart. :thumbsup:
Samir R: leaving this thread open until 24h stable. If oscillation stops, we'll roll-back temporary settings gradually and propose long-term autoscaler tuning.
Carla N: Closing loop: current status 21:54 UTC — 0 429s reported in last 15m, 95p latency down to 350ms. Will keep monitoring.
